Main article: [1955 French Makalu expedition](/wiki/1955_French_Makalu_expedition "1955 French Makalu expedition")

Makalu was first summited on May 15, 1955, by [Lionel Terray](/wiki/Lionel_Terray "Lionel Terray") and [Jean Couzy](/wiki/Jean_Couzy "Jean Couzy") of a French expedition led by [Jean Franco](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Franco_(alpiniste) "fr:Jean Franco (alpiniste)"). Franco, [Guido Magnone](/w/index.php?title=Guido_Magnone&action=edit&redlink=1 "Guido Magnone (page does not exist)") and [Gyalzen Norbu](/wiki/Gyalzen_Norbu "Gyalzen Norbu") Sherpa summitted the next day, followed by Jean Bouvier, Serge Coupé, Pierre Leroux and André Vialatte on the 17th. This was an amazing achievement at the time, to have the vast majority of expedition members summit, especially on such a difficult peak. Prior to this, summits were reached by one to two expedition members at most, with the rest of teams providing logistical support before turning around and heading home. The French team climbed Makalu by the north face and northeast ridge, via the saddle between Makalu and Kangchungtse (the Makalu-La), establishing the standard route.[[6]](#cite_note-baume-7)[[7]](#cite_note-AJ-8)

An ascent without oxygen was attempted by the [1960–61 Silver Hut expedition](/wiki/1960%E2%80%9361_Silver_Hut_expedition "1960–61 Silver Hut expedition") but neither of the two attempts succeeded.

The employment of these weapons in lower level conflict would be likely to escalate the situation, uncontrollably, to an intensity which could be vastly disproportionate to the original aggravation. The use of [ICBMs](/wiki/ICBM "ICBM") and [SLBMs](/wiki/SLBM "SLBM") is not, therefore, a rational or credible response to provocations which, although serious, are still less than an immediate threat to national survival. Almost all Asian religions have philosophical character and Asian philosophical traditions cover a large spectrum of philosophical thoughts and writings. [Indian philosophy](/wiki/Indian_philosophy "Indian philosophy") includes [Hindu philosophy](/wiki/Hindu_philosophy "Hindu philosophy") and [Buddhist philosophy](/wiki/Buddhist_philosophy "Buddhist philosophy"). They include elements of nonmaterial pursuits, whereas another school of thought from India, [Cārvāka](/wiki/C%C4%81rv%C4%81ka "Cārvāka"), preached the enjoyment of the material world. As of 2012, Hinduism has around 1.1 billion adherents. The faith represents around 25% of Asia's population and is the largest religion in Asia. However, it is mostly concentrated in South Asia. Over 80% of the populations of both India and Nepal adhere to Hinduism, alongside significant communities in Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and [Bali](/wiki/Bali "Bali"), Indonesia. In many of these cases, the "subcontinents" concerned are on different [tectonic plates](/wiki/Plate_tectonics "Plate tectonics") from the rest of the continent, providing a geological justification for the terminology.[[67]](#cite_note-Molnar2015-68) [Greenland](/wiki/Greenland "Greenland"), generally considered the [world's largest island](/wiki/List_of_islands_by_area "List of islands by area") on the northeastern periphery of the [North American Plate](/wiki/North_American_Plate "North American Plate"), is sometimes referred to as a subcontinent.[[68]](#cite_note-69)[[69]](#cite_note-FarmerCook2013-70) This is a significant departure from the more conventional view of a subcontinent as comprising a very large peninsula on the fringe of a continent.[[65]](#cite_note-Baldwin-66)

After an operation in Istanbul ends in disaster, Bond is missing and presumed to be dead. In the aftermath, questions are raised over M's ability to run the Secret Service, and she becomes the subject of a government review over her handling of the situation. The Service itself is attacked, prompting Bond's return to London. His presence assists MI6's investigation in uncovering a lead, and Bond is sent to Shanghai and Macau in pursuit of a mercenary named Patrice. There, he establishes a connection to [Raoul Silva](/wiki/Raoul_Silva "Raoul Silva"), a former MI6 agent who was captured and tortured by Chinese agents. Blaming M for his imprisonment, Silva sets in motion a plan to ruin her reputation before murdering her. Bond saves M and attempts to lure Silva into a trap, and while he is successful in repelling Silva's assault, M is killed. Bond returns to active duty under the command of the new M, Gareth Mallory.

Garrett's inauguration ceremony was held on September 18, 2015, on the [Arts Quadrangle](/wiki/Cornell_Central_Campus#Arts_Quadrangle "Cornell Central Campus") of [Cornell University](/wiki/Cornell_University "Cornell University").[[22]](#cite_note-22) She delivered her inaugural address in front of the iconic statue of [Ezra Cornell](/wiki/Ezra_Cornell "Ezra Cornell"). She spoke of "the spirit of Cornell that frames our journey" and stressed the importance of the faculty as the foundation of the university; students as partners in the voyage of discovery; and the university's growing presence in New York City as a source of opportunity.[[16]](#cite_note-inaug-16) Garrett said that the recruitment, development and retention of the best faculty remained Cornell University's paramount priorities. She also spoke of focusing on the residential undergraduate experience, defining as a community the shared intellectual experience all Cornell students should encounter.[[16]](#cite_note-inaug-16) And she pointed to the opportunities inherent in the university's dual footprint, in Ithaca and [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), urging all of Cornell's colleges to connect with [Cornell Tech](/wiki/Cornell_Tech "Cornell Tech") in new collaborations.[[16]](#cite_note-inaug-16)

Following the ceremony, the university hosted a picnic on the [Agriculture Quadrangle](/wiki/Cornell_Central_Campus#Agriculture_Quadrangle "Cornell Central Campus"), inviting [Ithaca](/wiki/Ithaca,_NY "Ithaca, NY") citizens as well as the campus community. The [Cornell Dairy](/wiki/Cornell_Dairy "Cornell Dairy") prepared 450 gallons of its newest ice cream flavor, 24 Garrett Swirl.[[16]](#cite_note-inaug-16) Later in the day, Garrett moderated a panel on democracy and inequality in [Bailey Hall](/wiki/Bailey_Hall_(Ithaca,_New_York) "Bailey Hall (Ithaca, New York)"), bringing together eminent faculty to explore how inequality interacts with immigration, access to education and health care, job creation and economic opportunity.[[23]](#cite_note-23)
